note: Rugby league's built-in earlier seasons (docs/design/rugby-league.md, "Earlier seasons"): the 2008 NRL season from Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition's own database, every player checked against the Rugby League Project's 2008 records; and the seasons 2009 to 2024 (`method` "computed"), which no game rated, computed from NRL.com's match centre ("Computed seasons"), whose `list` is the club's NRL.com nickname and `rlp` its Rugby League Project slug that season; `nrlcom` names each NRL.com team id's club (today's id), the same in every season. Each map in `maps` serves the seasons whose clubs share its grounds (its `note` says how; "nrl" is today's map, built from scripts/data/nrl-teams.json, which its seasons must equal). node scripts/sync-rugby-league-seasons.mjs writes scripts/data/rugby-league-seasons/<id>.json from the inputs pinned in scripts/data/rugby-league-seasons-sources.json; node scripts/build-rugby-league-seasons.mjs builds each season's clubs; node scripts/build-club-maps.mjs --league=nrl builds each era's map from `teams` and `maps`. `teams` lists every club of a season by the database's name for it (`list`) and the Rugby League Project's (`rlp`, its first-grade season page, whose slug the season before shares, read only to say why a player is left out; `nyc`, its National Youth Competition one): `franchise` is today's club, `id` the season's own where the club has been renamed or moved since, `ground` where it played its home games (a ground it still plays at under its present name), `base` where a club that shared its ground trained, and `home` the [lon, lat] its territory grows from (English Wikipedia's coordinates). `nations` are the season's World Cup nations, by the database's name, the game's nation id, RLP's World Cup squad heading and its Test team code: the sync checks their squads, but the season fields clubs only (docs/design/rugby-league.md, "Earlier seasons"); `carriedOver` the database's national squads that are older editions' and are not read; `nameFixes` a name the database spells with a character no name has.

maps.note: The sixteen of 2008 at their grounds of 2008 (`teams`), in 2009 too: the Bulldogs as "Bulldogs" from Sydney Olympic Park, the Storm at Olympic Park Stadium.
Canterbury-Bankstown again by name, still training at Sydney Olympic Park until it went back to Belmore in October 2011; the Storm at AAMI Park from its opening in 2010.

The Bulldogs grow from Belmore Sports Ground. A ground keeps its name of 2012 through the era (rule R3): Dairy Farmers Stadium, 1300SMILES Stadium by naming rights from 2013; the Sydney Football Stadium of 1988, Allianz Stadium by naming rights from 2012. The Eels keep Parramatta Stadium while it was rebuilt (rule R1: ANZ Stadium in 2017 and 2018; the new Western Sydney Stadium, on its site, from 2019), and so do the Roosters in 2019 (the SCG).

The Cowboys at the North Queensland Stadium (Queensland Country Bank Stadium) from 2020. The Roosters keep their own ground while it was rebuilt (rule R1: the SCG until the new Allianz Stadium opened in August 2022); the Warriors and the Storm keep theirs through COVID-19 (rule R2: the Warriors at Gosford in 2020 and 2021 and Redcliffe in 2022, the Storm on the Sunshine Coast in 2020). The Eels at the Western Sydney Stadium, CommBank Stadium today.
Today's clubs at today's grounds: the Dolphins join in 2023, and the Rabbitohs trained at the Heffron Centre from April 2023. Today's map, built once.

2008.name: Bulldogs
2008.era: The club played as the Bulldogs from 2000 to 2009, Canterbury-Bankstown again from 2010; it shared its ground with the Rabbitohs and moved its training and offices from Belmore Sports Ground to Sydney Olympic Park, beside the ground, early in 2008 (English Wikipedia, Belmore Sports Ground).

2008.name: Melbourne Storm
2008.era: The Storm played at Olympic Park Stadium until AAMI Park opened in 2010; the stadium was demolished in 2012.

2008.name: North Queensland Cowboys
2008.era: The Cowboys played at the Willows Sports Complex in Kirwan, then Dairy Farmers Stadium, until the North Queensland Stadium opened in 2020.

2008.name: Parramatta Eels
2008.era: Parramatta Stadium was demolished in 2016; Western Sydney Stadium stands on its site.

2008.name: South Sydney Rabbitohs
2008.era: The Rabbitohs shared their ground with the Bulldogs. Redfern Oval was the club's training ground from 1988 until it moved to the Heffron Centre in 2023; the council rebuilt it during 2008 and the club returned to it in 2009 (English Wikipedia, Redfern Oval). Where it trained during the rebuild is not recorded: it grows from Redfern.

2008.name: Sydney Roosters
2008.era: The Sydney Football Stadium of 1988 was demolished in 2019; Allianz Stadium stands on its site.

2008.name: Wests Tigers
2008.era: The Tigers played their 2008 home games at Accor Stadium (4), Campbelltown and Leichhardt Oval (3 each, RLP); they grow from Concord Oval, as today.
